newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks limp lower in muted session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks limp lower in muted session.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed lower on profit-taking Tuesday with turnover at token levels ahead of a pivotal tax debate in Congress, dealers said.

"Nobody wants to trade much until there is news on the congressional debate of austerity reforms," said bolsa secretary and independent broker Luis Corsiglia. "Some people who started selling yesterday wrapped up their business today, while buyers turned more cautious."
The weighted MerVal index .MERV shed 0.8 percent to 534.53, after rallying 4.3 percent since Thursday, while floor volume shrank by nearly half from Monday to 11.2 million pesos.
The lower house of Congress Wednesday night starts debate of a controversial tax package designed to help close Argentina's fiscal gap.

The measures have been watered down since they were aired by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez one month ago and while investors remain somewhat wary of congressional action, there should be enough consensus by now for approval, dealers said.

"Common sense says they should pass, because Congress is aware of the need to mend fiscal accounts," said Corsiglia. "Some people will argue they hamper economic growth, but there should be enough votes to secure approval."
He said the markets would next focus on the 1997 budget, "which is crucial to define the economic outlook and will be closely screened by the International Monetary Fund."
Traders said the IMF's tentative support for Argentina's new fiscal goals fueled market gains Monday.
"After today's slip the MerVal is likely to test resistance tomorrow again at 540, where it faltered Monday, but that ceiling could prove pretty strong," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
He forecast local stocks and bonds would also continue to move in tandem with the markets of New York.
In the session the broad market fell 0.7 percent, with winners whipping losers 30 to eight and 20 issues ending flat.
Over-the-counter volume dwindled to 57.9 million pesos against Monday's healthy tally of 10.3 million.

The main-tier standout was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which surged 7.3 percent on buyout speculation. The only two other MerVal gainers were textile firm Alpargatas and holding firm Comercial del Plata, up 0.9 percent and 0.4 percent each.
Among top losers oil firm Sol Petroleo fell 3.8 percent and Ciadea and Sevel shed 2.2 percent and 1.9 percent.
